subject: Velocity: Platinum Apps latency & error-rate operational briefing
messages:
From: Kim Lewis <kim.lewis@platinumapps.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <partner-sre@platinumapps.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PLAT-2389: sudden latency and 5xx surge (Nov 19)

Hi Ava,

We're seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and a jump in 5xx error rate from ~0.4% to ~6% starting ~08:45 PST this morning. Throughput dropped as retries kicked in, and our user-facing queue depth spiked. Dashboard attached (dashboard_snapshot_nov19.png) and I attached a short log extract (platinum_error_log_20261119.txt).

Impact: our payment flow timeouts are spiking and customers are reporting failures on checkout. This is affecting two of our top markets. We need immediate remediation and a clear ETA for a stable state.

Can we get an urgent call and a plan? If you can, please include an exec contact — our CS director Kim Lewis is on this thread and SRE is looped.

Thanks,
Kim
Kim Lewis
Director of Platform Reliability
Platinum Apps

Kim — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the artifacts. We're seeing the same signals in Redwood telemetry. I'm spinning up an incident bridge now and will start with containment steps while we triage root cause.

Immediate actions I'm asking for now:
- Activate fallback routing to the smaller instance family (routed to RDW-fallback-1) for non-critical traffic (we'll keep payments pinned to dedicated nodes for now)
- Temporary traffic shaping on Platinum traffic to reduce concurrency to 70% while we stabilize
- Capture KV cache metrics and node-level GPU memory stats (Dev, can you pull these ASAP?)

Proposed 30-minute exec/tech bridge at 09:35 PT. I will post bridge link and runbook shortly.

Ava Chen

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Exec war-room: Platinum Apps outage cadence (09:35 bridge)

Quick tech update from node triage:
- Symptom: KV cache churn + repeated evictions on serving pool rdw-prod-42/43. Observed OOM cycles on a subset of GPU instances which is triggering request retries and 503s from the runtime.
- Error rate: peaked at 6.2% at 08:55, now 3.7% after initial fallback routing.
- Root cause hypothesis: an uncommon request pattern (very long prompt lengths + high beam count) causing memory blowout on quantized kernel path.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:15–09:45):
1) Enabled fallback routing to RDW-fallback-1 for non-payment traffic (reduced load on prod nodes).
2) Disabled quantization-specific kernel for model variant v3.7 (forces non-quant path) to avoid pathological memory behavior.
3) Increased KV cache capacity and pinned high-frequency keys for Platinum tenant for 30m.
4) Rolling restart scheduled for rdw-prod-42/43 at 10:00 PT to clear kernel state (will be throttled to avoid capacity cliffs).

Next steps: monitor error rate and tail latency for 30m post-restart. If still above thresholds, we'll increase Dedicated pool and consider short-term priority burst capacity.

Dev
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, SRE Team <partner-sre@platinumapps.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Status update: service stabilization actions and ETA (PLAT-2389)

Kim — quick customer-facing status:
- What we did (9:15–10:05): enabled fallback routing for non-critical traffic, applied temporary traffic shaping, disabled quantization-specific kernel for affected model variant, and executed a rolling restart on two problematic nodes.
- Current state (10:10): error rate down to ~0.9% and tail latency reduced by ~30% vs. peak. Payment flows are trending to normal for most users; a small percentage may see retries while caches warm.
- ETA: we expect full stabilization within the next 45 minutes; we'll confirm by 11:00 PT.

Action items for customer: please confirm if you saw improved success rates on your end and whether you can accept a short window of degraded throughput during the next 30–45 minutes while caches complete warm-up.

We will follow up with a formal incident timeline and RCA within 48 hours and a proposed credit if we fall short of SLA commitments.

Thanks for your patience — we'll stay on the bridge and post rolling updates.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Kim Lewis <kim.lewis@platinumapps.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Status update: service stabilization actions and ETA (PLAT-2389)

Marissa / Ava — thanks. We can confirm improvement on our side: 5xxs reduced to ~0.8% and checkout success rate is back to expected levels. We saw a brief blip during the rolling restart but overall customer impact is limited now.

Next: we'd like a formal postmortem including the kernel/quantization interaction, and a proposal for how Redwood will avoid regressions (tests, guardrails, or automated fallbacks). We'll also open a formal request for SLA credit under our contract (PLAT-2389).

Appreciate the rapid response and clear comms.

Kim Lewis
Director of Platform Reliability
Platinum Apps
